title: Home-grown food
paragraphs: We all need to eat, and when we go to buy food at the supermarket, we’re spoilt for choice in the range of items available that can be turned into a delicious meal. But we often purchase food that’s been mass-produced and that’s travelled many miles before it ends up on our plate. So for some, growing their own food is a better option – and it tastes good too!

From growing vegetables in little pots on your balcony to tending to a small plot of land, called allotments, there are many ways to produce home-grown food. Allotments are a typically British idea, and they give people with a small or no garden, a space to plant and nurture fruit and vegetables. It can be backbreaking work digging, weeding and watering the soil, but the result is fresh, organically grown produce, contributing to our ‘five-a-day’ diet.

The recent Covid-19 pandemic lockdown means demand for allotments has seen a renaissance. Miriam Dobson from the University of Sheffield told the BBC that people with allotments have been spending a lot of their time on their plots, growing plenty of fresh fruit and veg – which, at times, have been challenging to source in supermarkets. She says “Coronavirus has… highlighted to people the fragility inherent within our globalised food system. In a time of crisis, interest in self-sufficiency rises.”

But for those with limited space, a solution to grow your own veg lies closer to home – using pots. Once you can lay your hands on some compost, you can plant seeds. Sheila Brand lives in a third-floor flat in Rotterdam. She has managed to grow tomatoes and aubergines and is already harvesting raspberries. She told the BBC watching the plants grow “is very exciting: 'Oh it's got a new leaf!' ”

As well as the benefits of saving money and enjoying tasty food, gardener Mark Ridsdill-Smith says “growing your own from a balcony or window ledge not only improves your wellbeing and immediate environment, you can actually grow a lot of veg.” So, maybe it’s time for us all to get planting and develop our green fingers!

vocabulary.entry: spoilt for choice /spɔɪlt fɔː tʃɔɪs/ 选择太多而难以取舍
vocabulary.example: We were spoilt for choice at the restaurant with so many delicious dishes on the menu.
vocabulary.translation: 那家餐厅菜单上的美味菜品太多，我们都不知道选什么好了。

vocabulary.entry: mass-produced /ˌmæs prəˈdjuːst/ adj. 大规模生产的
vocabulary.example: Most of the toys on the market are mass-produced in factories.
vocabulary.translation: 市场上的大多数玩具都是工厂大规模生产的。

vocabulary.entry: option /ˈɒpʃn/ n. 选择
vocabulary.example: There are several options available for solving this problem.
vocabulary.translation: 解决这个问题有好几种选择。

vocabulary.entry: balcony /ˈbælkəni/ n. 阳台
vocabulary.example: She likes to sit on the balcony and read books on sunny afternoons.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在晴朗的午后坐在阳台上看书。

vocabulary.entry: allotment /əˈlɒtmənt/ n. （用于种植的）租用地
vocabulary.example: He rents an allotment to grow vegetables for his family.
vocabulary.translation: 他租了一块地，为家人种植蔬菜。

vocabulary.entry: tend to /tend tuː/ 照料；打理
vocabulary.example: She spends her weekends tending to her garden.
vocabulary.translation: 她周末都用来打理自己的花园。

vocabulary.entry: nurture /ˈnɜːtʃə/ v. 培育；培养
vocabulary.example: The farmer nurtures the young plants carefully until they are strong enough.
vocabulary.translation: 农夫细心培育幼苗，直到它们长得足够茁壮。

vocabulary.entry: backbreaking work /ˈbækbreɪkɪŋ wɜːk/ 繁重累人的工作
vocabulary.example: Building the stone wall by hand was backbreaking work for the villagers.
vocabulary.translation: 手工砌石墙对村民们来说是一项繁重的活儿。

vocabulary.entry: weed /wiːd/ v. 除草
vocabulary.example: I need to weed the flower bed before the weeds get too big.
vocabulary.translation: 我得在杂草长得太大之前给花坛除草。

vocabulary.entry: organic produce /ɔːˈɡænɪk ˈprɒdjuːs/ 有机农产品
vocabulary.example: The supermarket sells a variety of organic produce from local farms.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市售卖来自当地农场的多种有机农产品。

vocabulary.entry: five-a-day diet /faɪv ə deɪ ˈdaɪət/ 每天五种蔬果的饮食结构
vocabulary.example: Doctors recommend a five-a-day diet to maintain good health.
vocabulary.translation: 医生建议每天摄入五种蔬果，以维持身体健康。

vocabulary.entry: renaissance /rɪˈneɪsns/ n. 复兴；再兴起
vocabulary.example: There has been a renaissance of interest in traditional crafts in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来，人们对传统手工艺的兴趣再度兴起。

vocabulary.entry: fragility /frəˈdʒɪləti/ n. 脆弱性
vocabulary.example: The fragility of the ecosystem becomes obvious after the natural disaster.
vocabulary.translation: 自然灾害过后，生态系统的脆弱性就显现出来了。

vocabulary.entry: inherent /ɪnˈhɪərənt/ adj. 内在的；固有的
vocabulary.example: There is an inherent risk in this kind of investment.
vocabulary.translation: 这类投资本身就存在固有的风险。

vocabulary.entry: globalised food system /ˈɡləʊbəlaɪzd fuːd ˈsɪstəm/ 全球化食品体系
vocabulary.example: The globalised food system connects farmers and consumers all over the world.
vocabulary.translation: 全球化食品体系将世界各地的农民和消费者联系在了一起。

vocabulary.entry: self-sufficiency /ˌself səˈfɪʃnsi/ n. 自给自足
vocabulary.example: The small village aims to achieve self-sufficiency in food production.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小村庄致力于实现粮食生产的自给自足。

vocabulary.entry: lay your hands on /leɪ jɔː hændz ɒn/ 得到；获得
vocabulary.example: I've been trying to lay my hands on that rare book for years.
vocabulary.translation: 多年来我一直试图找到那本珍本书。

vocabulary.entry: compost /ˈkɒmpɒst/ n. 堆肥
vocabulary.example: We make compost from kitchen waste and garden trimmings.
vocabulary.translation: 我们用厨余垃圾和花园修剪下来的枝叶制作堆肥。

vocabulary.entry: harvest /ˈhɑːvɪst/ v. 采收；收获
vocabulary.example: The farmers harvest wheat in late summer every year.
vocabulary.translation: 农民们每年夏末收割小麦。

vocabulary.entry: wellbeing /ˈwelbiːɪŋ/ n. 健康；幸福
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is essential for physical and mental wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动对身心健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: window ledge /ˈwɪndəʊ ledʒ/ n. 窗台
vocabulary.example: She placed a pot of flowers on the window ledge.
vocabulary.translation: 她在窗台上放了一盆花。

vocabulary.entry: green fingers /ɡriːn ˈfɪŋɡəz/ 园艺天赋
vocabulary.example: My grandmother has green fingers and can grow almost anything.
vocabulary.translation: 我奶奶很有园艺天赋，几乎什么都能种活。

sentences.chinese: 因此对有些人来说，自己种植食物是更好的选择——而且这样种出来的食物味道也很不错！

sentences.chinese: 租用地是颇具英国特色的产物，它能给那些花园面积小或者根本没有花园的人，提供一块种植和培育蔬果的场地。

sentences.english: It can be backbreaking work digging, weeding and watering the soil, but the result is fresh, organically grown produce, contributing to our ‘five-a-day’ diet.
sentences.chinese: 翻土、除草、浇水这些活儿虽然繁重累人，但收获的是新鲜的有机蔬果，能助力我们实现“每天五种蔬果”的健康饮食目标。

sentences.english: The recent Covid-19 pandemic lockdown means demand for allotments has seen a renaissance.
sentences.chinese: 最近新冠疫情的封锁措施，让人们对租用地的需求迎来了一次复兴。

sentences.chinese: 谢菲尔德大学的米里亚姆·多布森向英国广播公司表示，拥有租用地的人们在自家地块上投入了大量时间，种出了很多新鲜蔬果——而这些蔬果有时在超市里是很难买到的。她指出：“新冠疫情……

sentences.english: She says “Coronavirus has… highlighted to people the fragility inherent within our globalised food system.
sentences.chinese: 让人们意识到我们全球化食品体系内在的脆弱性。

sentences.english: In a time of crisis, interest in self-sufficiency rises.”
sentences.chinese: 在危机时期，人们对自给自足的兴趣会日益高涨。”

sentences.chinese: 但对于空间有限的人来说，在家种植蔬菜的解决办法其实很简单——用花盆就行。

sentences.english: Once you can lay your hands on some compost, you can plant seeds.
sentences.chinese: 只要能弄到一些堆肥，就可以播种了。

sentences.chinese: 希拉·布兰德住在鹿特丹一栋公寓的三楼，她成功种出了番茄和茄子，现在已经开始采收树莓了。

sentences.english: She told the BBC watching the plants grow “is very exciting: 'Oh it's got a new leaf!' ”
sentences.chinese: 她向英国广播公司表示，看着植物生长的过程“非常令人兴奋：‘哇，它又长出一片新叶子啦！’”

sentences.chinese: 除了省钱和享用美味食物这些好处外，园丁马克·里兹迪尔-史密斯表示：“在阳台或窗台上自己种植蔬果，不仅能改善身心健康和周边环境，实际上还能收获不少蔬菜呢。”

sentences.english: So, maybe it’s time for us all to get planting and develop our green fingers!
sentences.chinese: 所以，或许现在正是我们开始播种，培养自己园艺天赋的时候了！
